summary: This revision empirically cross-tabulates calibration method (raw softmax, temperature scaling, deep ensembling, ensemble+temp-scaling) against conformal nonconformity-score choice (LAC vs. APS) on a synthetic 6-class MLP task standing in for an LLM classifier, asking which factor dominates conformal prediction-set size. Compared to v1, it adds 10-seed replication for all headline numbers, corrects a v1 arithmetic error in the LAC calibration-effect spread, retracts an overstated 'ensembling worsens calibration' claim, and adds a noise/class-overlap sensitivity sweep showing the paper's own headline ranking (score-choice dominates calibration-method effect on set size) reverses at low class overlap (sigma=1.2). The core findings are that temperature scaling robustly fixes ECE (13x reduction, far outside seed noise), ensembling does not fix and may mildly-but-not-robustly worsen ECE, calibration method has no detectable effect on LAC set size but a real ~0.55-class effect on APS set size, and switching LAC to APS changes set size by ~1.9-2.5 classes (3.4-4.5x the robust APS calibration effect) under default settings only.
strengths:
- I independently re-ran both multiseed_experiment.py and sweep_experiment.py end to end; every headline number in Tables 3.1-3.3 and 3.5 reproduced bit-for-bit against results_multiseed.json and results_sweep.json (e.g. ECE 0.1386->0.0103, LAC set size 0.9077-0.9069 across methods, sigma=1.2 APS calib effect 2.4247 vs. score-switch 1.7407), and the section 3.4 ratio (1.88-2.48 / 0.55 = 3.4-4.5x) checks out arithmetically
- Genuinely responsive revision: it addresses all three concrete round-1 criticisms (single-seed results, an arithmetic error inflating the '4-60x' headline ratio, and no sensitivity analysis) with real re-computation rather than cosmetic rewording, and explicitly retracts the v1 claim that ensembling 'robustly' worsens ECE once the 0.005 gap is shown to be smaller than one seed-to-seed std (0.009)
- The added sensitivity sweep (Sec 3.5) is a real stress-test of the paper's own headline claim rather than a token addition, and it actually falsifies the claimed generality (dominance reverses at sigma=1.2) -- reporting a result that undercuts your own abstract is a strong honesty signal
- The LAC floor-effect / empty-set finding (9-10% of points get empty prediction sets at nominal 90% coverage, invisible from the coverage number alone) is a concrete, well-quantified, and non-obvious observation
weaknesses:
- The paper never uses a real LLM anywhere (disclosed, but still the central limitation): the title and framing throughout ('for LLM-Style Classifiers,' 'Practitioners building LLM systems...') claim relevance to LLM confidence estimation, yet the entire empirical base is a 6-way Gaussian MLP with 12% label noise, and Sec 3.5 itself demonstrates the qualitative ranking is regime-dependent -- which weakens rather than strengthens the claimed transfer to real, high-cardinality, highly-peaked LLM logit distributions
- The sensitivity sweep that drives the paper's most interesting new finding (the sigma=1.2 reversal) uses only 3 seeds per config versus 10 for the main results, and no seed-level std is reported for the sweep table (Table 3.5 has point estimates only), so the reader cannot judge how close to the reversal boundary the default sigma=1.8 configuration sits, or whether the 2.4247 vs. 1.7407 gap at sigma=1.2 would survive at n=10
- The core contribution remains narrow after the revision: one factorial design (2 calibration axes x 2 conformal scores x 1 synthetic family) plus a 2-parameter sweep, with no RAPS comparison (acknowledged as future work) and no non-LLM real dataset that could have added external validity cheaply; the 'no paper cross-tabulates this' gap claim is checked only against the cited LLM-era literature, not against the older general conformal-prediction literature where calibration-vs-efficiency studies are more likely to already exist
questions:
1. Would the sigma=1.2 reversal (APS calibration effect > score-switch effect) survive at 10 seeds, given the sweep currently uses only 3 seeds per config and reports no variance for Table 3.5?
2. Is there a principled reason low class overlap causes temperature scaling to affect APS's cumulative-mass ranking so much more (raw 2.64 -> temp-scaled 5.07 classes), beyond the 'near-deterministic softmax outputs' intuition given in Sec 3.5 -- would this same mechanism appear with a peakier, high-cardinality LLM-like output distribution, or does it specifically depend on having only 6 classes?
3. Given RAPS is explicitly flagged as unimplemented future work, do you have even an informal expectation of whether it would close enough of the LAC/APS set-size gap to threaten the paper's central 'score-choice dominates' framing?
